question: What is the primary substance that accumulates on teeth and hardens into calculus?
explanation: Dental plaque is a sticky bacterial film that builds up on teeth and calcifies into hard deposits if not removed daily. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why is mouth care an important nursing job and not just for looks?

options.A: It speeds up skin wound healing
options.B: It replaces the need for antibiotics
options.C: It stops germs from causing lung and body infections

explanation: You've got this! Keeping the mouth clean stops bad bacteria from traveling down into the lungs or blood, preventing serious sickness. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h1)

question: How many permanent teeth does a normal adult have?
explanation: A full set of permanent adult teeth numbers 32, which includes the wisdom teeth at the back! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the main protective job of saliva in the mouth?

options.C: Fighting germs and keeping the mouth moist
options.D: Holding loose teeth firmly in the jaw

explanation: Saliva is amazing—it contains natural germ-fighters and moisture that protect your mouth tissues from getting overloaded with bacteria. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h2)

question: Good mouth care helps prevent which major complication in patients on breathing machines (ventilators)?
explanation: Spot on! When patients are on ventilators, keeping their mouth clean prevents them from breathing in harmful germs that cause lung infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: How does proper oral care indirectly support a patient's physical healing process?

options.A: By stimulating the production of red blood cells
options.B: By increasing the body temperature to fight off germs
options.C: By replacing the requirement for intravenous fluids
options.D: By improving comfort and encouraging adequate food intake

explanation: A clean, comfortable mouth enhances taste and reduces oral pain, making it easier for patients to eat and maintain nutrition. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the medical name for a dry mouth caused by certain drugs or illness?
explanation: Xerostomia is just the clinical word for dry mouth. It happens when saliva drops, making the mouth more prone to infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which patient is at the highest risk for mouth breakdown and infections?

options.A: An active patient who brushes three times a day
options.B: A walking patient with steady blood pressure
options.C: An unconscious patient on a breathing machine
options.D: A young adult healing from a sprained ankle

explanation: Unconscious patients can't clean their own teeth, and their open mouths dry out quickly, putting them at high risk for infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which mouth condition shows up as creamy white, fungal patches?
explanation: Oral candidiasis (often called thrush) is a fungal overgrowth that leaves white patches, especially common when immunity is low. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the main cause of early-stage gum inflammation (gingivitis)?

options.A: The salivary glands making too much spit
options.C: Plaque building up and irritating the gums

explanation: It all starts with plaque! When plaque sits along the gumline, it irritates the gums and causes that red, swollen feeling. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h5)

question: What position should you put an unconscious patient in when cleaning their mouth?

options.A: On their side with the head turned
options.C: Flat on their back with chin up
options.D: Sitting straight up in a chair

explanation: Safety first! Placing an unconscious patient on their side lets any cleaning fluid drain safely out of the mouth instead of going into the lungs. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why should you never put your bare fingers inside an unconscious patient's mouth during care?

options.B: The patient might bite down suddenly by reflex
options.C: Gloves will easily tear on adult teeth
options.D: The patient might accidentally swallow your finger

explanation: Never take chances with bare fingers! Unconscious patients can bite down without warning, so always use padded tongue blades or tools. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is it smart to line the sink with a towel when washing removable dentures?

options.B: To stop cleaning chemicals from staining the basin
options.C: To protect the dentures from breaking if you drop them
options.D: To soak up water splashing from the tap

explanation: Dentures are surprisingly fragile and slippery when soapy. A simple towel in the sink cushions them if they take a tumble! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is the correct way to store artificial dentures overnight?

options.A: Wrapped in a dry paper towel on the bedside table
options.B: Soaked in pure bleach until morning
options.D: In a labeled container with clean water or soaking solution

explanation: Keep them moist! Storing dentures in water or cleaning solution overnight stops the material from warping and keeps them safe. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h7)

question: How often should a person get a brand new toothbrush?
explanation: Bristles bend and lose their scrubbing power over time, and germs love to hide on old brushes. Swap it out every 3 to 4 months! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h8)

question: Why do dentists recommend check-ups every six months?

options.A: To get professional teeth whitening only
options.B: To catch cavities and gum trouble early
options.C: To stop wisdom teeth from growing
options.D: So you can stop brushing at home

explanation: Regular check-ups help catch small issues before they turn into painful cavities or big infections. Prevention is key! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h8)
